heading: ## Project intent
reason: Consumer-tier: both published surfaces resolve to ONE `python -m livespec_dev_tooling.checks.<slug>` entrypoint set — the `run-check` composite Action's namespace template, the local `just check-<slug>` recipes, and the shipped canonical modules — which is what "consumers MUST use both surfaces in concert" means where a consumer can observe it (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-fx4fap).

heading: ## Architecture
reason: Consumer-tier: drives a shipped check module over a clean fixture and over one carrying an injected violation, asserting the section's Python-package surface contract in both directions — exit 0 on pass, non-zero on fail with a structured stderr diagnostic naming the failure (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-fx4fap).

heading: ## Definition of Done
reason: Unit-tier: asserts the DoD's tree-decidable bullets against the aggregate the merge gate actually runs — every shipped canonical check is a `just check` target, the ruff lint/format, pyright and 100%-coverage gates the DoD names by tool are targets too, and every shipped check carries its 1:1 mirrored test (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-fx4fap).

heading: ## Non-goals
reason: Consumer-tier: each v1 non-goal read as a consumer meets it — no publishing mechanism in the packaging config or the shipped CI surface, no livespec requirement on the installed distribution and no `livespec` import in any shipped module, neither livespec-private check hosted in the canonical set, and no `templates/library/` tree (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-fx4fap).

heading: ## CLI surface
reason: Consumer-tier: the section's SECOND paragraph — the three operational CLI modules (`install_commit_refuse_hooks`, `install_worktree_pack`, `install_no_shadow_ledger`) held to the same semver-stable `python -m` invocation contract as the checks: each ships inside the packaged directory, exposes a zero-argument `main`, carries the `__main__` guard without which `python -m` runs nothing, and is the SINGLE source of the canonical body it writes — exercised end to end on the neutral-hook installer, which writes bytes byte-identical to its carried constant, is idempotent, and no-ops rather than hard-erroring on a declared-absent role key. The first paragraph's argv / `--help` / no-network clauses are covered at `tests.consumer.test_cli_shape` and `tests.consumer.test_no_network_io` (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-jj7cx2).

heading: ## Exit-code table
reason: Consumer-tier: the table is read FROM the spec and diffed against the integer constants every shipped check's and workflow check's `main()` returns, so an undocumented code — or a deleted table row leaving a module returning it — convicts; the reserved-range rule is asserted on the same set (a code above the table's highest row must also be named in its own module docstring). A companion test drives a shipped check over a clean and a violating consumer fixture, asserting exit `0` on the clean tree and a documented non-zero code with the structured stderr finding on the other (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-jj7cx2).

heading: ## Shared check inventory
reason: Unit-tier: the partition asserted as the mechanical property the section says it is — no module under the two deliberately-placed sibling directories (`workflow_checks/`, `charters/`) reaches the filesystem-derived canonical set, the two declared workflow-check members ship where that placement puts them, `lint`/`format`/`complexity` ship no slug module, and the hand-maintained `baseline` profile stays a subset of the canonical set carrying its two Conformance-Pattern Verifiers. The livespec-private half is covered at `tests.consumer.test_non_goals` (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-jj7cx2).

heading: ## Consumer configuration schema
reason: Consumer-tier: the schema exercised through the loader a consumer's checks read it with, against fixture trees — the `[tool.livespec_dev_tooling]` block governs alone (a decoy `.livespec.jsonc` layout never reaches the loader), and declaration-presence is recorded distinctly from value across a fixture pair whose parsed values agree. Companion tests assert this consumer declares every member of `REQUIRED_ROLE_KEYS` and that a bare `[]` on a UNION key is rejected at load with a diagnostic naming the key and every legal spelling, while staying legitimate on a CLEAN key (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-jj7cx2).

heading: ## Composite Actions wire contract
reason: Consumer-tier: the three shipped Actions held to the wire a consumer passes them by name — every documented input declared, every REQUIRED one still required, and every optional one carrying the exact documented default (a default is the value an omitting caller receives and never sees, so `500`/`1`/`30`/`3900` drift silently fleet-wide) — plus the declared `token` output and `run-check`'s step list still naming the `python -m livespec_dev_tooling.checks.<slug>` invocation form (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-jj7cx2).

heading: ## Reusable workflows wire contract
reason: Consumer-tier: the named minimum-set member `reusable-check-matrix.yml` held to the wire its callers depend on — the `checks` input still REQUIRED and typed `string` (the caller passes a JSON-array string), the strategy still matrixing over `fromJSON(inputs.checks)`, and each matrix entry still running the `run-check` composite Action, without which the input is accepted and silently ignored. heading: ## Consumer compat block — pin-and-bump policy
reason: Consumer-tier: this library's own `compat` block — the section binds it as a consumer — asserted as filed under the consumer's own library name with both REQUIRED fields and an EXACT field set, since 'the block contains only non-sensitive version metadata' and `.livespec.jsonc` MUST NOT carry secrets. heading: ## Cross-repo coordination automation surface
reason: Consumer-tier: the four-member reusable workflow inventory held to its declared wire — required inputs still required, the `release_url` required/optional asymmetry between the dispatcher and the bump-pin handler, the two threshold defaults (`1`, `24`), and the App-token secrets each shim threads by `secrets: inherit`. Companion tests assert the surface fires only the two declared `repository_dispatch` event types (an undeclared type fires into silence, since GitHub matches no workflow and does not error) and that §"Self-hosting"'s three consumer shims ship and DELEGATE rather than inline the coordination logic (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-jj7cx2).

heading: ## Semver discipline
reason: Unit-tier: the BUMP RULES asserted as applicable rather than the enumeration as resolvable (that is `tests.consumer.test_semver_stable_surface`, the constraints.md invariant). The MAJOR rule names 'removing or incompatibly reinterpreting a recognized `[tool.livespec_dev_tooling]` key', so the loader's recognized key set and the specification's role-key inventory are diffed in both directions with the spec's own carve-outs (`REQUIRED_ROLE_KEYS` normative; `repo` documented as NOT loader-implemented). heading: ## Versioning
reason: Unit-tier: the lockstep asserted across the records that carry it — the `pyproject.toml` version equals the `.release-please-manifest.json` entry outright, and `v<version>` is among the tags wherever the checkout carries any (a tagless clone is a can't-read, not a violation). A companion test asserts `release-please` is the only tool positioned to write them: a second writer must first NAME the manifest, and no shipped module or justfile recipe does (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-jj7cx2).

heading: ## Runtime
reason: Consumer-tier: the declared floor and the actual one, which fail at different moments. `requires-python` (what a consumer's resolver reads), ruff's `target-version` and pyright's `pythonVersion` must name the same release, and every shipped first-party module is re-parsed with `ast.parse(feature_version=(3, 10))` so a module carrying post-floor grammar cannot be imported on the interpreter the distribution promises (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hhp4og).

heading: ## Dependencies
reason: Consumer-tier: `[project]` carries no `dependencies` key AND the installed distribution's Requires-Dist (a separate artifact, which a build-backend or dynamic-metadata dependency would reach without touching the config) is empty; the vendored `returns` / `structlog` imports every check makes resolve from `livespec_dev_tooling/_vendor/`, which is what makes the zero-dependency claim honest; and ruff, pyright and pytest carry exact `==` pins under `[dependency-groups].dev` (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hhp4og).

heading: ## No network I/O
reason: Consumer-tier: drives a shipped check end-to-end with every `socket` entry point replaced by a refusing double and asserts it still exits 0, then asserts the double is live. This is the constraint's stated REASON — determinism against the working tree alone, regardless of network availability — and the leg the import scan in the same file cannot reach, since a reach made through a helper or a lazily-imported module names no forbidden root in the check's own AST (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hhp4og).

heading: ## Semver discipline
reason: Consumer-tier: resolves each surface element `contracts.md` enumerates against the tree at the version the packaging config declares — both `python -m` invocation sets, every composite Action's `runs:` wire, every reusable workflow's `workflow_call:` trigger, and the importable detector API's non-empty registry and glob set. An element that no longer resolves IS a break that landed without the MAJOR bump the constraint requires, which is what covers the removals a diff-based bump classifier misses (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hhp4og).

heading: ## CLI shape
reason: Consumer-tier: the contract at all three layers it can break — every canonical check's `main` is callable with no arguments, no check declares a positional argparse argument, and two fixture trees differing ONLY in their `[tool.livespec_dev_tooling]` blocks resolve to different configurations while argv is held identical and bare, which is what proves configuration comes from the working directory rather than argv (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hhp4og).

heading: ## Self-application
reason: Unit-tier: wiring is not application. A repo can carry every canonical slug in its aggregate and every recipe pointed at the pinned shared module while its `[tool.livespec_dev_tooling]` block aims the scan where the shipped modules are not — every check then passes by inspecting nothing and raises no error. This resolves the configured universe the way the checks resolve it and asserts each shipped check module is inside it, both by containment under a declared source tree and through `iter_py_files`, the walker the shape checks actually use (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hhp4og).

heading: ## CI matrix shape
reason: Consumer-tier: the constraint's own reason is that a consumer's branch protection names individual matrix entries as required checks, so the entry set is asserted event-independent — the workflow triggers on `pull_request` and on `push` to master alike, the retired zero-`.py` subsetting mechanism and the trigger-level path filters that would subset the same way are absent, no job in `ci-green`'s `needs:` set carries a job-level `if:`, and every matrix target is a literal `check-<slug>` (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hhp4og).

heading: ## Boundary
reason: Unit-tier: the section is a ROUTING TABLE, and a misroute is otherwise silent — nothing in the toolchain objects to a section written into the wrong spec file, and for one class the silence is total: `heading_coverage` SKIPS `## Scenario:` headings in every file EXCEPT `scenarios.md`, so a scenario parked elsewhere is exempt from the registry and reads exactly like a scenario nobody wrote. Each bullet is asserted in the direction it constrains — the named content is in the file the bullet names, the content the boundary routes AWAY is absent from this file, acceptance scenarios live only where the gate reads them, and a heading this file shares with a sibling (today `## Self-application`) must CITE that sibling rather than restate it, since two definitions of one rule drift. Companion assertions at `tests.spec.test_specification_boundary` cover the scenario-placement and cross-reference halves (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hj42cw).

heading: ## Test-Driven Development discipline
reason: Unit-tier: the STAGE each named gate is wired at — the part of the section no check can defend, because a check cannot observe whether it was invoked. `red_green_replay` must be a commit-msg command (the `TDD-Red-*`/`TDD-Green-*` trailers it reads live in the message, which does not exist at pre-commit) and must receive lefthook's `{1}` message-file argument: without it the gate silently falls back to its `origin/master..HEAD` range mode, which passes on a branch whose landed commits already carry trailers, so it stays green while judging nothing. The companion `test_the_source_and_test_pairing_gate_is_wired_at_pre_commit` asserts the pairing bullet's other named surface, whose hook invocation is its ONLY deciding one — inside `just check` `commit_pairs_source_and_test` passes VACUOUSLY on an empty staged diff (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hj42cw).

heading: ## Testing approach
reason: Unit-tier: the H3 "Scenario-tier coverage" rules applied to this repository's own registry, in the three directions no shipped check covers here. RESOLVABILITY is the mapped one: a node id must name a test that exists, which `heading_coverage` deliberately does not check (that direction was armed ahead of adoption, reddened three consumer repos and was reverted, livespec-dev-tooling-jel7) — adopting it repo-locally is the adoption-then-arming order, and it stops an id left behind by a rename from reading as coverage. Companions assert GRANULARITY (one row per scenario; the check diffs triples as a SET, so a duplicate row is invisible to it while giving the heading two answers) and that every declared `scenario_tiers` prefix names a real directory, since a typo'd prefix does not fail — it silently stops matching (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hj42cw).

heading: ## Linter rule set
reason: Unit-tier: the enumerated ruff categories are READ FROM THE SECTION and diffed against `[tool.ruff.lint].select`, so the test cannot drift from the list it enforces; an unselected category produces no findings and a lint run missing a whole category is indistinguishable from a clean one. The direction is containment, not equality, because the tree deliberately wires a 28th category (`BLE`, with its reason recorded at the array) that the section does not enumerate. Companions assert the section's own arithmetic (each bullet's parenthesised count against the list it labels), that `ISC001` is the ONLY ignored rule, and — exactly, since the section is exact — the four pylint thresholds, the `ban-relative-imports` mode and the six banned APIs (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hj42cw).

heading: ## Typechecker rule set
reason: Unit-tier: strict mode plus the seven strict-plus diagnostics, read FROM the section's bullet list. Each is a line that can be deleted with nothing failing — the diagnostic falls back to its strict default (off, or a hint) and the class of defect it was elevated to catch starts shipping — so the assertion is that all seven are EXPLICITLY configured, six at `error`, and the seventh never weaker than `warning`. `reportImplicitStringConcatenation` sits at `warning` on livespec's documented li-xxjopf precedent, which the test pins as the ONE argued relaxation rather than blessing a second; the section's literal `= error` for it, and its `include` clause's `tests/` half (unmet: 1936 strict errors there today), are reported as spec-amendment findings on the PR instead of being encoded as though the spec said something weaker (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hj42cw).

heading: ## Code coverage thresholds
reason: Unit-tier: `exclude_also` asserted as SET EQUALITY against the list read from the section's own enumerating sentence — the direction the section demands ("No other exclusions are permitted without a propose-change cycle") and the one knob that makes the 100% floor cheaper to satisfy WITHOUT writing a test: an excluded line leaves both the numerator and the denominator, so an added pattern raises the reported percentage while lowering the tested fraction and the gate reports green either way. The companion `test_the_coverage_floor_is_the_full_line_and_branch_gate` asserts the floor itself and that `branch` measurement is actually on, without which every untaken `else` counts as covered (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hj42cw).

heading: ## Comment discipline
reason: Unit-tier: the section's mechanical half — the `ERA` ban on commented-out code and LLM scaffolding — asserted as ARMED rather than merely selected, over the actual `.py` files of the package and `tests/`. Selection is not arming, and this repository has already paid the difference: `pyproject.toml` records that excluding one hook file from ruff WHOLESALE via `extend-exclude` "took the `BLE001` backstop down with it", with nothing failing and ruff reporting a clean tree over a smaller tree than intended. So no `extend-exclude` glob may swallow a governed file and no `per-file-ignores` entry may list `ERA`/`ERA001` over one; the companion asserts the rule is selected at all. The line-number-anchor half is the shipped `comment_line_anchors` check, covered by its own paired unit suite (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hj42cw).

heading: ## Keyword-only arguments
reason: Unit-tier: the section's DATACLASS clause, which no shipped check enforces — `keyword_only_args` covers the `def`-level `*` separator and its own docstring defers `dataclass(frozen=True, kw_only=True, slots=True)` verification to "subsequent cycles" that have not run, so reading the two def-level gates as covering the section leaves this clause covered by a check that declines the claim. Asserted directly over the package's AST: a positionally-constructible record silently permutes its call sites when a field is inserted or reordered, and where the fields share a type the permutation still type-checks. It convicted one real offender on authoring (`checks/_primary_checkout_unreadable.CheckInputUnreadable`, two `str` fields), fixed in the same commit (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hj42cw).

heading: ## Structural pattern matching
reason: Unit-tier: the `<subject>` half of `case _: assert_never(<subject>)`, which the shipped `assert_never_exhaustiveness` check explicitly does not verify ("Subsequent cycles can tighten to verify the call's argument equals the match subject"). The argument is the whole mechanism: pyright narrows the SUBJECT to `Never` once every variant is handled, so a call pointed at any other expression computes that narrowing for a value nobody asked about — the arm still looks right, the shipped check still passes, and the exhaustiveness check silently stops checking. Nothing notices at runtime either, because `[tool.coverage.report].exclude_also` carries `case _:` and the arm is never measured (plan fleet-heading-coverage-convergence P2 burn-down, livespec-dev-tooling-hj42cw).
